Corollary
[Radial Distance Equals Riemannian Distance]

↗ prop:radial-geodesic-unique-minimizer 1. ch6:6.12

Let $(M,g)$ be connected and $p\in M$. On every open or closed geodesic ball centered at $p$, the radial distance (6.4) equals $d_g(p,\mathord \cdot )$.

Proof

\sketch It suffices to consider an open geodesic ball because each closed one lies in a larger open one. For any $x$ in the ball, the radial geodesic is minimizing by Proposition prop:radial-geodesic-unique-minimizer. Its velocity is $\partial _r$, which has unit length in both the Riemannian metric and normal coordinates, so its length is $r(x)$.

□
